outcome: No proof, disproof, or new theoretical argument about the infinitude of Kynea primes was found; only continued distributed-computing record searches (which do not bear on the existence question per §3.1) turned up, and their dates are inconsistent across secondary sources and mostly predate the window.
summary: Kynea numbers have the form (b^n+1)^2-2; a Kynea prime is a prime of this form. The question 'are there infinitely many Kynea primes?' is an existence/infinitude question, so under §3.1 it moves only when actually answered, and record searches (finding a larger example, extending a search bound) narrow where an answer could hide without touching the question. Searches turned up no proof or heuristic argument published since 26 January 2024, no disproof, and nothing resembling a resolution. What did turn up was a confused set of 'largest known Kynea prime' claims scattered across secondary/mirror sites (Googology Wiki, HandWiki, EverybodyWiki, prime-numbers.info): one snippet cites a 169,553-digit example by C. Emmanuel that other sources date to November 2005 (an early hand/CPU search, well before the frozen date and using the original discoverer's own search rather than anything new); another cites index n=852770 (513,419 digits) found by Ryan Propper in July 2019 using CKSieve/PrimeFormGW; yet another cites index n=661,478 (398,250 digits) from June 2016. These are mutually inconsistent snapshots of an aggregator table that is evidently not being kept current by any of the mirror sites, and none of the dates fall in the 26 Jan 2024–present window regardless. The authoritative record source, Prime-Wiki (rieselprime.de), returned repeated 503 errors during this research and could not be fetched directly, so I could not confirm the exact current record holder or date from the primary source; this is noted as a dead end. The underlying search effort is a MersenneForum-coordinated distributed sieving/PRP-testing project (CKSieve, PrimeFormGW, LLR-type primality tools) opened in December 2015 and still active, which is classical computer algebra / exhaustive-search infrastructure, not an AI system by any of the codes in §6.2 — a targeted search for AI or LLM involvement in Kynea prime searches returned nothing relevant. No AI system of any kind appears anywhere near this problem or its associated record-search community.
competing_reading: None of the 'largest known Kynea prime' claims found actually fall inside the research window, so there is no genuine candidate event to weigh against the open/no-change classification here; the only live ambiguity is which of the three inconsistent record claims (2005/2016/2019) is currently accurate, which affects no field in this record since none postdate 26 Jan 2024.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or heuristic/probabilistic argument (analogous to the standard conjectures for Mersenne/Cullen/Woodall-type primes) establishing infinitude, or a rigorous disproof; short of that, a reliable current snapshot of the Prime-Wiki Carol-Kynea table would at least pin down the present record holder, though that would still not change the open status.
